title: Grade 2 Math — Thu, Jun 12
description: Measurement — Day 4 of 5: Capacity units (mL and L)
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Which unit measures how much liquid a container holds?
questions.explanation: Capacity (how much a container holds) is measured in litres (L) or millilitres (mL).

questions.question: A medicine dropper holds about 5 ___.
questions.explanation: A medicine dropper holds a tiny amount — about 5 millilitres (mL).

questions.question: 1 litre = ___ millilitres.
questions.explanation: 1 L = 1000 mL. Just as 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.

questions.question: A bucket of water holds about 10 ___.
questions.explanation: A bucket holds a lot of water — about 10 litres (L).

questions.question: A teaspoon holds about 5 ___.
questions.explanation: A teaspoon holds a tiny amount — about 5 mL.

questions.question: Which holds MORE — 1 L or 200 mL?
questions.explanation: 1 L = 1000 mL. 1000 mL > 200 mL, so 1 L holds more.

questions.question: A water bottle holds 500 mL. How many bottles fill 1 L?
questions.explanation: 1 L = 1000 mL. 1000 ÷ 500 = 2. You need 2 bottles to fill 1 litre.

questions.question: Which tool do we use to measure liquids?
questions.explanation: A measuring jug has mL and L markings to measure how much liquid is inside.

questions.question: A small juice box holds 200 mL. Mum's juice carton holds 1 L. How much more is in Mum's carton?
questions.explanation: 1 L = 1000 mL. 1000 − 200 = 800 mL more in Mum's carton.

questions.question: Which would you use to measure milk for a recipe — mL or km?
questions.explanation: mL measures liquid. km measures distance. For milk, we use mL.

questions.question: A big pot holds 5 L of water. How many mL is that?
Half a litre is equal to ___ mL.
Which holds LESS — a cup (250 mL) or a bottle (1 L)?
questions.explanation: 250 mL < 1000 mL (1 L). The cup holds less.
